name: Dark Teal
lede: Dark Teal is a very deep blue-green, almost black, a shade down from [[teal]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a dark bluish green.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 carries a block at this position, number 165, dark bluish green, under 2 CIEDE2000 units from this swatch [1]. Wikipedia's own color list cites that ISCC-NBS block for its nearby entry, and the xkcd survey of 2010 later collected the plain descriptive phrase "dark teal" from the public [1].

No book in our library records who first drew the line at this exact depth of blue-green, so its coinage as a named color stays undocumented here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[kremlin]], [[deep-teal]] and [[samara]], at 2.9, 3.2 and 4.1 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 29 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Paul Gauguin's Tahiti scenes carry it most heavily, at nearly 66 times the archive's baseline rate, and his *Teuraheimata a Potoru* (1891) covers a third of its canvas with it [2]. It is most common in works from Realist and Post-Impressionist movements, and the word "Petrol" shares its canvases far more than chance [2]. Where it appears, it most often sits as a shadow color [2].
